chapter: Arranging for other bandleaders and closing talk
title: Standard big-band instrumentation, writing for fiddles, and end of the proceedings
summary: Horace wrote for the standard big-band instrumentation, a little for violins after studying at Damrosch in New York. The tape ends.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: One thing I want to bring just before this tape runs out, did you do much writing or did Fletcher for unusual instrumentation? I mean did -- like did you -- the guys double on flutes and occasionally oboes or things like that or --
No, mine was just the basic things.

-- like four trumpets, three trombones, five saxophones and everything. I wrote a little bit for fiddles, but I had to go to school a little bit. In fact, this is what you have to do. But mine was primarily like the instrumentation for the big bands, what they carried, originally had.
You say you went to school -- where and what?
Oh, in New York at Damrosch. I had to find out a few things in But that came in handy.
Our tape is about shot on this one.
